clue.text: Place without privacy where Selima perished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a situation where everything you do is watched
second meaning: Selima is the cat in Thomas Gray's ode who drowned in a tub of goldfish

explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's 'Ode on the Death of a Favourite Cat, Drowned in a Tub of Gold Fishes' tells of Selima, who fell in reaching for the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass fish tank is visible from every side, hence the idiom for a life lived in full public view.

clue.text: Best work seen before Neo's filling belly

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of what follows in the answer

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: the setter's contraction goes inside the word for belly, as stuffing fills it

parts.note: tum is informal for belly or stomach
Neo is the setter, so Neo's = 'I am' = I'M

explanation.surface: A setter's best work comes before a filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; 'Neo's' is 'Neo is', the setter saying I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the most favourable or ideal, a straightforward synonym for the best possible.

clue.text: Milling around is ancient reptile

indicators.note: crowds milling around move about in disorder, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something wandering about aimlessly turns out to be a prehistoric creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs were reptiles that lived many millions of years ago, a plain example of the description.

clue.text: Couple's part in white magic

indicators.note: the answer is a part sitting inside the next two words, spanning their join

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of white and the start of magic

explanation.surface: A pair's role in some benign spellcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is informal for two people in a romantic relationship, so a couple.

clue.text: Racecourse for chariots in Hull city

parts.note: hip and in both mean fashionable
a pod is the hull or husk of peas and beans
Rome is the city

explanation.surface: A chariot track in the English city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hull' looks like the Yorkshire city but is the husk of a pea; 'city' supplies the other city.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippodrome was the stadium for horse and chariot racing in ancient Greece and Rome.

clue.text: Extra time open to view

parts.note: over can mean extra, left over, as in 'over and above'

explanation.surface: Added minutes in a match are there for everyone to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and not concealed, the opposite of covert.

clue.text: Attract fish rising to sheltered side

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to draw a crowd is to attract it
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Luring fish up towards a sheltered bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the side away from the wind, so the one protected from it.

clue.text: Rob — he's mustard playing in holiday kit

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, moving into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Rob is keen and on form in his holiday clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mustard' here is old slang for keen or excellent, but it is only anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Knee-length casual shorts named after the island, a classic piece of tourist wear.

clue.text: Guys stopping a test drive wrecked trailer

indicators.note: the word for guys plugs a gap in the other letters, stopping it as a cork stops a bottle
a wrecked car is broken up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: guys means men

explanation.surface: Men interrupt a test drive and wreck the trailer being towed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a towed vehicle in this driving scene; it is the film preview.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a short promotional clip for a film, an example of a commercial promotion.

clue.text: Understanding French in marquee finally possible

parts.note: en is French for in
a marquee is a large tent

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of possible

explanation.surface: Communicating in French inside a big tent may at last be possible.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Fake groom died introducing tango

indicators.note: the grooming word has the tango letter introduced into it

parts.note: to preen is to groom oneself
Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A sham bridegroom dies while bringing in a tango.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to feign or put on a false show, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Silent addendum brings complaint

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay silent
PS, postscript, is an addendum to a letter

explanation.surface: A note added without comment leads to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' reads as a grievance; here it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, and mumps is a viral illness swelling the glands.

clue.text: Snake having bit in famous row

parts.note: a boa is a snake
a trace is a small bit

explanation.surface: A snake with a bit in its mouth caused a notorious argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is rowing; the Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is the best-known rowing match in Britain, hence a celebrated row.

clue.text: Way horse consumes good and bad meat dish

indicators.note: the horse word takes the good letter inside it, eating it

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat
food that has gone off is bad

explanation.surface: A street horse eats both good and rotten food in a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is a Russian dish of strips of beef in a sour-cream sauce.

clue.text: Cleaners ringing a doctor for 617 chaps?

indicators.note: the cleaners surround the other letters, forming a ring round them

parts.note: dusters are cloths for cleaning
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Cleaners surround a medic, apparently for a particular group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: No 617 Squadron RAF carried out the 1943 bouncing-bomb raid on German dams and became known by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The men of 617 Squadron were nicknamed after their wartime raid breaching the Ruhr dams.

clue.text: Version in which sea-water obeys Canute?

indicators.note: King Canute ordered the tide to go back; if it obeyed, the word would run backwards

parts.note: the tide is the rise and fall of sea-water

explanation.surface: An account in which the sea does what King Canute told it.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend has King Canute ordering the incoming tide to turn back; it did not.
explanation.definitionFit: An edit is a revised cut of a film or text, so a particular version of it.

clue.text: Forward subbed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ahead in development or position
second meaning: lent money, as in 'sub me a fiver', British slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Subbed' looks like sport or editing; in British slang to sub someone is to lend them money ahead of payday.
explanation.definitionFit: Advanced means progressed or ahead, and also describes money paid out as a loan beforehand.

clue.text: Fourth man went down hard

parts.note: the sun set, went down below the horizon

explanation.surface: The fourth person collapsed heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, after Adam, Cain and Abel, Seth was born, making him the fourth man in the Bible.

clue.text: Article about Sally Ann appearing in May?

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about, concerning
Sally Ann is a nickname for the Salvation Army, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A news piece about the Salvation Army being published in May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is the month on the surface but the surname of Theresa May, UK prime minister 2016-19.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of former British prime minister May, so the name that appears with it.

clue.text: Generous care of married male causing offence

parts.note: c/o, care of, on an envelope
odious means hateful, giving offence

explanation.surface: A married man in someone's care proves generous but offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous here means roomy or ample in size, and commodious means spacious.

clue.text: Opening gold reserve, single key to be inserted

indicators.note: the single and key letters are put inside the other pieces

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
ice means coolness or reserve of manner
I is the Roman numeral one
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Opening the gold vault with one key.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or aperture, especially a bodily one, so an opening.

clue.text: Old writer, accessible, banning current style in office

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: the current letter is banned, kept out of the word for accessible

parts.note: plain means clear and easy to understand

explanation.surface: An old author, approachable, rules out a modern workplace layout.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office has no dividing walls, a style of workplace layout.

clue.text: Where one sees stem and large stalk

parts.note: the stem is the forward timber of a ship's bow, found at the prow

explanation.surface: A plant stem and a large stalk seen together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stem' and 'stalk' look like botany; the stem is the front of a ship and stalk is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prowl is to move stealthily in search of prey, as a hunter stalks.

clue.text: Man going after a kiss in principle

indicators.note: the Man letters follow the earlier pieces

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: In theory, a man goes after a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth or basic rule, a founding principle.

clue.text: Northern girl left behind in US

parts.note: ass is American for backside

explanation.surface: A girl from the north stayed behind in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is the word for a young woman in northern England and Scotland.

clue.text: Rapid reiteration of note's lot more varied

indicators.note: the letters are varied, set in a different order

explanation.surface: Musical vibrato that gives many more variations.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo is a quick repetition of a single tone in music, giving a trembling effect.

clue.text: Say Sotheby's sale posh indeed?

indicators.note: split 'indeed' as 'in deed': the posh letter goes in the word for deed

parts.note: an action is a deed
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: An upmarket auction-house sale is posh, isn't it?
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'indeed' into 'in deed'. U for upper-class is from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotheby's is a famous auction house, so its sale is an example of a public sale by bidding.

clue.text: Lay waste to feudal land so unexpectedly

indicators.note: laying waste wrecks things, so these letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Without warning, an army devastates a medieval estate.
explanation.definitionFit: All of a sudden is an idiom meaning abruptly, without warning.
